source_record.title: Momentum Transfer
source_record.scope_note: Nine testable points split the seven handwritten bullets and nested timing examples without treating the notes as evidence.

summary.human_blocker: No qualifying governed participant dataset with synchronized bilateral six-axis grip wrenches is available.

critical_points.present_answer: Drift fractions exist only for a named observable, frame, decomposition, and event window; several model tiers close these ledgers, but no universal swing-level percentage exists.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Publish one common estimand table across all forward tiers and repeat it with measurement uncertainty on participant-held-out bilateral-wrench trials.
critical_points.falsifier: A registered drift contribution or its forward persistence vanishes, reverses, or is smaller than numerical or measurement uncertainty.
critical_points.data_gate: Common state/input/interface histories are available in models; qualifying governed human bilateral-wrench data are not.

critical_points.present_answer: Force-velocity angle, relative-link angle, signed contact separation, transverse differential force, reference point, and frame transport gate transfer sign, zero, and magnitude in declared analytical, planar, and reduced spatial models.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Repeat the frozen null and reversal atlas with subject-scaled articulated arms, calibrated grip compliance, distributed club dynamics, and held-out human geometry/wrench measurements.
critical_points.falsifier: A null or sign-reversing geometry does not null or reverse the proposed pathway beyond uncertainty or the result fails an independent engine.
critical_points.data_gate: Reduced-engine controls exist; subject-scaled scapular/arm/grip geometry and synchronized bilateral wrenches remain unavailable.

critical_points.present_answer: Casting is not one mechanism or event; distal-angle, distal-rate, wrist-angle, and event-window definitions can disagree, so no universal causal diagnosis is supported.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Pre-register multiple casting criteria and retain their disagreement while independently intervening on distal release, proximal acceleration, and proximal braking under matched work and delivery state.
critical_points.falsifier: A proposed casting mechanism changes sign or disappears under a plausible registered event definition or matched-state/work control.
critical_points.data_gate: Synthetic event definitions can be exercised now; causal human adjudication needs synchronized kinematics, wrenches, and impact outcomes.

critical_points.present_answer: Pointwise identical-state interventions show a nonmonotonic and sign-changing club-acceleration response; acceleration cannot be treated as a free or universally beneficial input.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Execute forward factorial proximal-acceleration interventions with matched work, peak load, and full delivery state across moving-base, spatial, and subject-scaled tiers.
critical_points.falsifier: The proposed early-acceleration benefit plateaus, reverses, or is explained by work, state, orientation, or load differences.
critical_points.data_gate: Pointwise and rotating-base model evidence exists; independent forward causal and human tests remain open.

critical_points.present_answer: Release timing changes geometry, work timing, and delivery in the tested models, but the selected timing is program-, model-, objective-, and constraint-dependent rather than universal.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Map viable release regions under factorial proximal drive/braking and distal actuation, multiple objectives, matched effort/load, phase uncertainty, and impact outcomes.
critical_points.falsifier: The apparent release advantage disappears under matched controls, reverses for a credible objective, or incurs an adverse orientation/load cost.
critical_points.data_gate: Several planar timing grids exist; spatial, subject-scaled, and participant-held-out impact tests remain open.

critical_points.present_answer: Mechanical passivity at an instant does not imply low preparation or neural timing demand. In the registered common-phase planar screen, the clock policy retained 4/5 robust task-viable phase points and 45 ms of contiguous width, versus 1/5 and no multi-point span for the delayed/noisy state trigger; this falsifies a state-trigger timing-volume advantage in that model, not in people.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Repeat the common-phase viable-volume comparison with independently identified observers, continuous phase sampling, spatial impact outcomes, subject scaling, and participant-held-out perturbations.
critical_points.falsifier: The drift-mediated policy has an equal or smaller viable region, worse lower-tail result, or greater delay/phase sensitivity than its comparator.
critical_points.data_gate: The moving-base two-hand planar comparison is executed under common speed, face/path, force, effort, and numerical guards; identified human delays, spatial impact, and participant perturbation trials remain unavailable.

critical_points.present_answer: No tested policy has established self-correction. The expanded common-phase screen observed no sustained half-error recovery in any of 60 policy/load/phase cases, so neither clock nor state triggering has a recovery-qualified viable region in this model.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Estimate continuous attraction regions with independently identified observers, stronger feedback families, saturation and external-contact disturbances, then test held-out spatial and human recovery without hidden force or effort cost.
critical_points.falsifier: Perturbations do not decay, viable-set return is not more probable, or any benefit requires an undeclared load increase.
critical_points.data_gate: Small and expanded planar recovery screens exist; independently identified spatial observers and governed human perturbation data remain open.

critical_points.present_answer: Energy-, work-, and load-controlled planar results are nonmonotonic and retain both favorable and adverse higher-rate outcomes, rejecting proximal velocity as a standalone maximization rule at those tiers.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Perform independent forward rate and acceleration interventions with full-delivery-state matching, then search for interior optima across spatial, subject-scaled, and held-out human tiers.
critical_points.falsifier: A proposed monotonic benefit contains a plateau, interior optimum, reversal, adverse load, or dependence on the matching rule.
critical_points.data_gate: Planar dose-response evidence exists; causal spatial and human validation remain open.

critical_points.present_answer: Five declared slack classes have now been exercised separately under two synthetic excitations with class-specific engagement, mechanical passivity where applicable, energy closure, delayed-control boundaries, and local sensitivity audits. No global benefit, necessity, intentionality, or delivery advantage is supported; one scalar output nearly confounds contact disengagement with the biological-compliance surrogate.
critical_points.decisive_next_test: Embed one mechanical class at a time in moving-base, two-hand, and spatial delivery models under matched work, load, and state; add a stateful play operator and subject-specific tissue models; then use independent contact, shaft, tendon, activation, and bilateral-wrench measurements to test class identification.
critical_points.falsifier: A proposed benefit disappears when slack classes are separated, violates passivity or energy closure, or is non-identifiable from the available measurements.
critical_points.data_gate: Synthetic constitutive, passivity, and local-sensitivity evidence exists; calibrated contact, shaft, muscle-tendon, activation, and human grip-state measurements remain open.
